description: Complete Frontend UI with multi-screen session flow - Welcome/folder picker, Leader selection, Chat planning interface, Plan approval, Worker dashboard, and Status bar. Replaces the existing minimal index.html with a full single-page application using vanilla HTML/CSS/JS that implements the complete user flow from the prototype.html design.
steps: Step 1: Create the full frontend at crates/synergy-ui/dist/index.html. The app must implement a multi-screen SPA with these screens/states: (a) WELCOME screen - landing page with app branding, 'Open Folder' button triggering a folder picker dialog, and 'Create New Project' option. (b) LEADER_SELECT screen - shown after folder is selected; displays cards/list of available adapters from adapters.toml (opencode, aider, claude-cli, codex-cli, cursor, kiro, vscode, windsurf) with their type (cli/gui) and description; user picks one as Leader. (c) PLANNING screen - chat interface where user talks to Leader; user types requests, Leader responds with plans; shows message bubbles (user/assistant/system). (d) PLAN_REVIEW screen - displays parsed tasks from Leader's plan in a checklist; user can Approve or Request Changes. (e) EXECUTING screen - the main 3-column layout from prototype.html: Progress panel (left, ~10%), Workers grid (center, ~55%), Leader chat (right, ~35%). Shows real-time worker output via xterm.js terminals, task progress, worker status dots, activity log. (f) COMPLETE screen - summary of completed session.

Step 2: Implement screen navigation state machine in JS. Track current screen state (welcome, leader_select, planning, plan_review, executing, complete). Transitions: welcome->leader_select (on folder picked), leader_select->planning (on leader chosen), planning->plan_review (when plan is detected), plan_review->executing (on approve), executing->complete (when all tasks done).

Step 3: Welcome screen implementation - Show Synergy logo/branding, project folder path input with 'Browse' button. The Browse button calls Tauri's dialog API (window.__TAURI__.dialog.open with directory:true) or falls back to a text input. Store selected folder path in app state.

Step 4: Leader selection screen - Fetch available adapters via a new Tauri command 'get_adapters' (to be added in FEAT-002). Display them as clickable cards showing: adapter id, type badge (CLI/GUI), description. On selection, store chosen adapter and transition to planning screen.

Step 5: Planning/Chat screen - Full chat interface with message list (scrollable), textarea input, send button. Messages rendered as bubbles: user messages right-aligned in accent color, assistant messages left-aligned in surface color, system messages centered and dim. When user sends a message, call 'send_to_leader' Tauri command (FEAT-002). Listen for 'leader-output' Tauri event to receive Leader's streamed response. Detect when Leader's response contains a numbered/bullet plan (use same regex pattern as backend: lines matching /^\s*\d+[.)]/). When plan detected, show 'Review Plan' button that transitions to plan_review screen.

Step 6: Plan Review screen - Parse the Leader's plan text into individual task items. Display as a numbered list with checkboxes. Show two buttons: 'Approve & Execute' (calls 'approve_plan' command from FEAT-002, transitions to executing) and 'Request Changes' (returns to planning screen with a pre-filled message asking for revisions).

Step 7: Executing screen (main dashboard) - Implement the 3-column layout matching prototype.html design: Left panel (Progress): task checklist with status icons, progress bar, worker status summary, activity log. Center panel (Workers): 2x3 grid of worker cards each containing an xterm.js terminal instance with live output, status dot, proxy IP label, current task label. Right panel (Leader): ongoing chat with Leader showing batch reports and review status. Status bar at bottom showing: leader name, workers busy/total, proxy status, task progress.

Step 8: Wire up real-time events - Listen for 'worker-output' Tauri event and route chunks to the correct worker terminal. Listen for 'session-state-changed' event (FEAT-002) to update progress panel. Poll get_state every 1 second as fallback for state updates. Listen for 'leader-output' event for Leader chat messages during execution.
Step 9: Complete screen - Show session summary: total tasks completed, time elapsed, any escalated/failed tasks. Offer 'New Session' button to return to welcome screen.

Step 10: Implement mock mode for browser preview (no Tauri available) - detect if window.__TAURI__ is undefined and use mock functions that simulate the flow with fake data. This allows the UI to be previewed in a browser without the Tauri backend.

Step 11: Style everything using the dark theme CSS variables from prototype.html (catppuccin-mocha inspired: --bg:#1e1e2e, --accent:#89b4fa, etc). Ensure the UI is responsive within the Tauri window (min 1024x640 per tauri.conf.json). Use JetBrains Mono for terminals, Inter for UI text. Include the xterm.js and xterm-addon-fit libraries via CDN links (they're already referenced in the existing index.html).
acceptance_criteria: The file crates/synergy-ui/dist/index.html exists and contains a complete SPA with all 6 screens
Welcome screen shows folder picker UI and transitions to leader selection on folder choice
Leader selection screen displays adapter cards and transitions to planning on selection
Planning screen provides chat interface with message rendering and plan detection
Plan review screen shows parsed tasks and approve/revise buttons
Executing screen shows 3-column layout with worker terminals, progress panel, and leader chat
Status bar shows session info (leader, workers, tasks, progress)
Mock mode allows browser preview without Tauri backend
All Tauri invoke calls use correct command names matching FEAT-002 additions
CSS uses dark theme consistent with prototype.html design language
verification: Read crates/synergy-ui/dist/index.html and verify it contains all screen implementations
Verify the file references correct Tauri command names (init_session, get_state, get_adapters, select_folder, choose_leader, send_to_leader, approve_plan)
Verify xterm.js terminal setup code exists for worker panels
Verify state machine transitions are implemented in JavaScript
findings: File is 904 lines. All 6 screens implemented with state machine transitions. Mock mode simulates full flow with fake adapters and task execution. Regex plan detection uses /^\s*(\d+)[.)]\s+(.+)$/ matching backend pattern. xterm.js terminals are created on entering executing screen and disposed on new session. The frontend references these Tauri commands: get_adapters, choose_leader, send_to_leader, approve_plan, get_state. Events listened: worker-output, leader-output. Braces fully balanced (234/234). Extra ) in raw paren count is from regex char class [.)] which is valid JS.
